content: The Christopher and Dana Reeve Foundation (CDRF) is a charitable organization based in Short Hills, New Jersey. Its primary mission is to discover treatments and cures for paralysis caused by spinal cord injuries and other neurological disorders. Additionally, the foundation is committed to enhancing the quality of life for individuals living with disabilities. The foundation traces its origins to the American Paralysis Foundation, which was established in 1982. In 1995, actor Christopher Reeve sustained a spinal cord injury during a horse-riding accident, leaving him quadriplegic. Following his injury, Reeve sought the assistance of the organization, lending his name and financial support. Over time, the organization was renamed the Christopher Reeve Paralysis Foundation and later became the Christopher Reeve Foundation. By early 2006, the foundation had awarded over $64 million in research grants and more than $8 million in quality-of-life grants. After Christopher Reeve's death in October 2004, his widow, Dana Reeve, assumed the role of Chair of the Foundation. Tragically, Dana Reeve passed away 17 months later, in March 2006, due to lung cancer. Following her death, Peter D. Kiernan III became the Chair of the Foundation. On March 11, 2007, the foundation announced a name change to the Christopher and Dana Reeve Foundation, marking the first anniversary of Dana Reeve's passing. According to the foundation, this change was intended to honor the partnership, courage, and compassion of the Reeves. The mission of the Christopher and Dana Reeve Foundation is to cure spinal cord injuries by funding innovative research and to improve the quality of life for individuals living with paralysis through grants, information, and advocacy. In June 2006, the foundation launched a public awareness campaign by selling Superman Tags. These dog tags featured the iconic Superman S-Shield logo and the foundation's motto, Go Forward. All proceeds from the sale of these tags were directed toward the foundation's efforts to find treatments and cures for paralysis. Warner Bros. allowed the foundation to use the Superman logo royalty-free for the duration of the campaign, which ended in February 2008. The foundation aimed to replicate the success and popularity of the Lance Armstrong Foundation's LIVESTRONG wristbands. Several celebrities participated in the campaign and were tagged, including Brandon Routh (who portrayed Superman in Superman Returns), Kate Bosworth (Lois Lane in Superman Returns), Dean Cain (Superman in Lois and Clark: The New Adventures of Superman), Erica Durance (Lois Lane in Smallville), David Boreanaz, Robin Williams, and Ray Romano. Christopher Reeve's legacy will continue to be remembered.
